title: Merging of independently growing domains generically produces nesting

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Merging of independently growing domains generically produces nesting

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Nesting can arise from random initial conditions through progressive annihilation of randomly placed elements: in essentially any system where domains grow fairly independently and then progressively merge, an overall nested pattern resembling a river-tributary tree forms, even when domain boundaries move as random walks.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 7: Mechanisms in Programs and Nature

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And indeed in essentially any system where there are domains that grow fairly independently and then progressively merge the same basic overall nesting will be seen.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 7, “Mechanisms in Programs and Nature”; section “Origins of Simple Behavior” (from p. 351), p. 359. Scope: cellular automata such as rules 184 and 110 and other domain-coarsening systems from random initial conditions

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch07-22: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.71

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Domain mergers naturally generate explicit trees whose nesting can be measured in simulation. Public rules and software permit broad tests including the named cellular automata. Finite model ensembles cannot settle the unrestricted universality wording.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Simulate a preregistered ensemble of coarsening systems with independently growing domains, including random-walk boundaries, and quantify hierarchical nesting in merger trees. A system satisfying the premises but consistently lacking nested merger structure would refute the generic assertion.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Nested resemblance needs a quantitative threshold.

Finite runs may miss asymptotic coarsening behavior.

Essentially any system is an unbounded universal claim.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.7

data adequacy: 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Annihilating and coalescing boundaries are a standard stochastic process, and the named cellular automata are small computations. The genealogy of mergers is a concrete object, so the nested-tree description can be confirmed or replaced by a counterexample inside the stated class. That is a computation, not a new observation of nature.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Simulate rules 184 and 110 and a family of domain models whose boundaries annihilate on contact, including random-walk boundaries, and test whether the merger genealogy is a nested tributary tree. A nested merger tree across that family would support the claim; a broad class of independently growing, then merging, domains whose genealogy is not nested would refute the essentially any quantifier.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Nesting in rule 110 is approximate once the localized structures are coarse-grained.

Fairly independently has to be defined before the family of systems is closed.
